differences.title: 1. PRIMARY USE CASE
differences.leftDesc: Best for applications requiring a dedicated database server and network access.
differences.rightDesc: Ideal for mobile apps, desktop apps, and simple websites with local data.

differences.title: 2. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Handles large datasets and high concurrency with robust features for growth.
differences.rightDesc: Best for smaller, localized datasets; not designed for high concurrency.

differences.title: 3. CONCURRENCY CONTROL
differences.leftDesc: Multi-Version Concurrency Control ensures better performance with multiple users.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on file-level locking, which can cause write contention.

differences.title: 4. DATA INTEGRITY
differences.leftDesc: Strong ACID compliance with advanced features like foreign keys and triggers.
differences.rightDesc: Provides ACID compliance but with fewer advanced features and potential edge cases.

differences.title: 5. SETUP & MAINTENANCE
differences.leftDesc: Needs installation, configuration, and ongoing administration by a DBA.
differences.rightDesc: Self-contained, no server to manage, database is a single file.

differences.title: 6. NETWORK ACCESS
differences.leftDesc: Designed for client-server interaction over a network.
differences.rightDesc: Directly embedded in the application, accessed locally.

differences.title: 7. COMPLEX QUERIES
differences.leftDesc: Supports complex joins, window functions, and advanced SQL features.
differences.rightDesc: Supports standard SQL but may lack some advanced functionalities.
